mood.VERY_LOW: Even getting started may feel tiring today. Give yourself some room to rest, and we can think about studying again later.
mood.SERIOUS_DISTRESS: You do not have to carry this alone. Contact someone you trust now; if you may hurt yourself, call your local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department.
mood.LOW: Thinking about everything at once may feel tiring today. If you like, start with a few questions on a familiar topic and see how you feel before continuing.
mood.OKAY: You can begin without feeling especially motivated. Pick one topic for a short review, then decide whether you want to keep going.
mood.GOOD: While you feel good, we can make room for a topic you have been meaning to study. Give it one focused session, then see what feels clearer.
mood.GREAT: It is good to feel eager to study today. You could start with something that interests you or a topic you have been putting off, leaving room for a break too.

motivation.GOING: Your rhythm is holding. One small step today is enough. I'm here.

ghost.BELOW_PREVIOUS: A little behind this time, it happens. Don't dwell on one attempt; look at your trend. I'm here.

weekly.WEEKLY_FOLLOW_UP_RHYTHM: This step concerns your study routine. Task status is current; it is not compared with subject scores.
weekly.WEEKLY_FOLLOW_UP_NO_BASELINE: The source week has no score for this subject. A progress difference cannot be calculated from later records alone.
weekly.WEEKLY_FOLLOW_UP_WAITING: No new attempt taken after you added this task falls within this report's period.
weekly.WEEKLY_FOLLOW_UP_MEASURED: This is the first attempt after you added the task. It compares one attempt with the source week's average; the difference alone does not establish the recommendation's effect.

weekly.DEEP_FOCUS_MINUTES_FIRST: You focused for {current} minutes this week. There is no comparable record for the previous week.

weekly.DEEP_ACTIVE_DAYS_FIRST: You were active on {current} days this week. These records will form the next comparison.

weekly.DEEP_PLAN_TASKS_FIRST: You completed {current} tasks this week. There is no comparable record for the previous week.

weekly.DEEP_SUBJECT_STEADY: Your {subject} average stayed the same, across {count} attempts this week and {previousCount} the previous week.
weekly.DEEP_SUBJECT_EARLY: Your {subject} average is {net} net across {count} attempts. There is no attempt for this subject in the previous week.
weekly.DEEP_SUBJECT_NO_EXAM: There is no {subject} attempt this week. Your study activity is visible; a net change cannot yet be compared.

weekly.DEEP_EVIDENCE_COMPARABLE: There are {current} attempts this week and {previous} the previous week. Difficulty can vary; a net change alone cannot explain the effect of studying.

improvement_cycle.BASELINE_MISSING: The baseline mock exam is no longer available. Your task remains, but this loop's net change cannot be measured.
improvement_cycle.WAITING_PRACTICE: Your focus is in the plan. The next step appears after you complete the task or review a matching mistake.
improvement_cycle.WAITING_MEASUREMENT: The practice step is recorded. We will check the change in the next mock exam containing the same exam and subject.
improvement_cycle.RESULT: Your {subject} net moved from {baseline} to {followUp}, a difference of {delta}.

notebook_pattern.KNOWLEDGE_GAP: Most of your recent mistakes are topics you did not know. Review genuinely helps here.
notebook_pattern.RUSHING: You know the topic. Most of your mistakes are careless slips. Try slowing down and checking rather than re-studying.
notebook_pattern.READING: Most of your mistakes come from misreading the question. Reading the stem twice helps here.
notebook_pattern.DISTRACTOR: Distractors are catching you. Try forming your own answer before eliminating options.
notebook_pattern.TIME_PRESSURE: Most of your mistakes come from time pressure. Timing yourself per question is a good next step.
notebook_pattern.SECOND_GUESSING: You find the right answer and then change it. Trusting your first call is worth a try.
notebook_pattern.MIXED: Your mistakes do not point at one cause yet. The pattern will sharpen as a few more pile up.
